access_note: Dryad lists the 349.49 MB archive and a short README. DataCite specifies CC0 1.0 and the EDENext Europe study extent. The archive and individual rasters were not downloaded, so values, current projections and exact map bounds were not tested.
description: Environmental Research Group Oxford publishes nine population-proximity raster layers for the EDENext European study extent. Dryad lists 1 km GeoTIFF and GeoJPEG layers for rural, urban and total populations in 2005, 2030 and 2050, plus a README. Each cell represents nearby people weighted by distance over a 30 km neighbourhood, not only residents inside that cell. This can help health-service, emergency-response or exposure simulations place potential visitors near a locality and test future population patterns. DataCite records CC0 1.0. The 2030 and 2050 values are projections, not observed populations, and the 2013 deposit may not reflect later demographic revisions. The 349 MB archive was not downloaded, so its cell values, missing-data codes and map bounds remain unverified. A related catalogue record, WorldPop gridded population, describes population distribution itself; the proximity layers answer a separate neighbourhood-access question. A modeller should inspect the README and projection method before combining these layers with a service catchment or disease model.
